comments: Ceiling check, not a real deployable config: same architecture/hyperparameters as kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_cfar_damp_kernel3_finetune_dropout.json (0.3749/0.3529 val/test), but the CFAR detector is replaced by ground-truth dense annotation masks (kurals/dataset_process/oracle_detect_and_damp_dataset.py) to decide what native pixels survive flattening before pooling. This cheats with labels no real detector can access, so it measures the best possible downstream dice for the entire detect-then-flatten-then-pool approach family (CFAR, Gaussian peak-finding, or anything else). Ground truth flags far fewer pixels than CFAR did (0.0035% vs CFAR alpha=5's 0.092%) since dense annotations are near-single-pixel-per-target, so this is an even more aggressive flatten than either CFAR variant tried. If this loses to plain max-pooling (0.3757/0.3635), that's decisive: the contrast-dilution theory isn't what's gating downstream dice, and no smarter detector would help either -- ruling out further contrast-preservation variants (Gaussian peak-finding included) without needing to build and test each one.
